text.label: Demo report: fictional site "Harbourline Cargo", all data made up
text.headline: Release 4.0 [[breaks the quote form on phones]] and stops counting leads
text.lead: Desktop users can still request a quote, but on a 390 px phone the form is 690 px wide and the last fields sit off-screen. The form's success event no longer reaches GA4 either, so the drop in leads would go unseen. Fix those two before the next deploy; the rest can go into the backlog.
text.areasNote: Each bar is one area's checks: black passed, amber warnings, vermilion failed. All 11 areas were checked in this run.
text.areasH: Mobile and analytics fail; console, speed and copy need work
text.areasP: Scores 0-100 show how ready each area is for production: 100 minus points per finding, weighted by severity. Below 40 means broken where it matters.
text.flowsH: The quote flow breaks twice: on phones, and after sending
text.flowsP: The key visitor flows from the homepage to a quote request, a call and the German version. Forms were filled up to the submit button and never sent.
text.matrixH: {qw} quick fixes with high impact and low effort
text.matrixP: Each dot is a finding from the table below. Black dots are bugs, outlined dots are gaps in coverage or process, vermilion dots are the top 3.
text.bugsP: ICE = impact × confidence × ease (each 1-10). Observed means you can see it in a screenshot or a log; hypothesis means it still needs confirming.
text.nextH: Fix these three before the next deploy
text.nextP: For each: what is broken, when it counts as fixed, and which automated test proves it.
text.planH: All {n} findings: steps, expected, actual, evidence
text.planP: Every finding has steps to reproduce, expected and actual results, evidence, a fix and an automated test. The top 3 also list the fix options considered, a done-when threshold and a pre-mortem.
text.checkP: The short list to run after every release: tag, events, redirects, forms, texts, languages, sitemap, console and speed.
text.testsH: {tests} automated checks to rerun after every deploy
text.testsP: The checks never submit a form: the lead event is tested by firing the form's success event in the browser. Status "now" is the result of running the suite once during this audit.
text.testsCmd:
cd qa-tests
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
npx playwright test              # after every deploy
BROWSERS=all npx playwright test # + Firefox and WebKit (Safari)
text.dataH: Confidence is demo-level: every source here is fictional
text.dataP: In a real run these rows show which tools were used (browser, headless Playwright, PageSpeed, CMS, GA4) and which were missing. Each missing source lowers confidence, and an area that could not be checked shows as "not checked".
how: Checked the connected tools: browser, headless Playwright with three engines, PageSpeed Insights and a read-only WordPress connector.
Asked 4 start questions, each one skippable. One was skipped and replaced with a stated assumption.
Walked the key flows at 1280, 820 and 390 px. Read the console, network, dataLayer, sitemap and redirects, crawling politely at one request every 1.5 s.
Confirmed each known issue with our own evidence. Ranked findings by severity, then ICE, and added fix options, thresholds and a pre-mortem for the top 3.
Wrote a test for every bug, ran the suite once, and render-checked this report on desktop, tablet and phone.

kpis.l: Critical bugs, both on the quote flow

verdict.note: The site is up and desktop quotes work, but phone users cannot complete the form and no lead is measured. Hotfix both before the next deploy.

route.p: Works, but no GA4 tag on this template

bugs.t: Quote form is 690 px wide on a 390 px phone; last fields off-screen
Form success event no longer sends generate_lead to GA4
14 URLs from the old theme return 404 (no redirects)
"Customs brokerage" card shows the refrigerated-cargo text
GA4 tag missing on the /tracking/ page template
Mobile LCP 4.8 s: hero image is lazy-loaded
Quote button on /de/ still reads "Get a quote"
Sticky header may hide the #quote heading in Safari
Nobody runs post-deploy checks; this release went live untested

1.h: On a 390 px phone the quote form is 690 px wide, so visitors scroll sideways and miss the Email field.
1.m: No sideways scroll at 390 and 820 px; all 6 fields are reachable with one thumb.
1.t: Test T06 at phone and tablet widths, then one manual check on a real phone.

2.h: Since release 4.0 the form's success event fires, but nothing listens for it, so no lead reaches GA4.
2.m: A test lead appears in GA4 DebugView as generate_lead, marked as a key event.
2.t: Test T04 (synthetic success event, nothing sent).

3.h: Links to 14 pages from the old theme (ads, emails, Google) now land on a 404.
3.m: Each old URL 301-redirects in one hop to its new page.
3.t: Tests T09-T09c, plus Search Console's 404 report after a week.

steps: Open https://harbourline.example/ at 390 × 844 (iPhone 13/14 size).
Tap "Get a quote" to jump to #quote.
Try to reach the Phone and Email fields.
1.exp: The form fits in one column; no sideways scroll.
1.act: The form grid has three fixed 220 px columns (690 px in total). The page scrolls sideways and Email sits off-screen.

evid.t: documentElement.scrollWidth = 702 at innerWidth 390; form computed grid-template-columns: 220px 220px 220px

fix: In the theme CSS, change the form grid to repeat(auto-fit, minmax(14rem, 1fr)).
Set inputs to width: 100% and font-size: 16px to stop iOS zooming in.
Re-run T06, then check once on a real phone.
1.risk: Other forms on the site may share the class; check the contact page too.
alt: Hide the extra fields on phones: rejected, because sales need the route and the cargo type.
A separate mobile form: rejected, because two forms to maintain would drift apart again.
1.thr: T06 passes at 390 and 820 px, and no field needs a sideways scroll.
1.pm: It failed because the cache plugin kept serving the old CSS file. Purge the cache and bump the theme version in the same deploy.

steps: Open the homepage and wrap dataLayer.push to record events.
Fire the form's success event on the form element (synthetic; nothing is sent).
Wait 1.5 s, then read dataLayer and the /g/collect requests.
2.exp: generate_lead in dataLayer and a GA4 hit with en=generate_lead.
2.act: No new dataLayer entries. The old snippet listened on .wpcf7-form, which the new theme renamed.

evid.t: dataLayer +0 after synthetic success event; snippet selector .wpcf7-form matches 0 elements
WPCode snippet "lead-event" active, last edited before release 4.0

fix: Listen on document instead of a theme class: document.addEventListener('wpcf7mailsent', …).
Keep generate_lead marked as a key event in GA4.
Confirm in DebugView with one owner-sent test lead marked "TEST".
2.risk: Double counting if GTM also fires on the thank-you URL. Keep a single source for the event.
alt: Track the thank-you page view instead: rejected, because the form shows an inline message and has no thank-you URL.
Move all tracking to GTM: later, as a bigger change than this hotfix.
2.thr: T04 passes and DebugView shows generate_lead for the test lead.
2.pm: It failed because the snippet only loads on the homepage while the form also sits on /contact/. Load it site-wide and add T04b for /contact/.

steps: Take the old URL list from the previous sitemap (kept in the repo).
Request each URL at one request per 1.5 s.
Note the status and the final URL.
3.exp: Each old URL 301-redirects to its new page.
3.act: 14 of 60 old URLs return 404, all under /services/*.
fix: Add 301s in the Redirection plugin: /services/sea/ → /sea-freight/, and so on (14 rows).
Re-run T09-T09c and the sitemap check.
3.risk: Redirect chains: point each rule straight at the final URL.
alt: One regex rule /services/(.*) → /$1-freight/: rejected, because 3 slugs do not follow the pattern.
Server-level rules: possible, but the team edits redirects in WordPress.
3.thr: T09-T09c pass, and Search Console's 404 count for /services/* falls to 0 within a week.
3.pm: It failed because the cache served old 404s. Purge the cache after adding the rules.
3.code:
/services/sea/   -> /sea-freight/   301
/services/road/  -> /road-freight/  301
/services/air/   -> /air-freight/   301
# ... 11 more rows from the old sitemap

steps: Open the homepage.
Read the "Customs brokerage" card in "Freight solutions for every route".
fix: Ask the owner for one line on the customs service.
Replace the text in every language version.

steps: Open /tracking/.
Look for gtag.js with the measurement id and a /g/collect hit.
5.exp: The same GA4 tag as on other pages.
5.act: No tag on this page; the tracking template has its own header.php.
fix: Call wp_head() in the tracking template's header, or move the tag into a site-wide snippet.
Add T03b to the suite.

steps: Run PageSpeed Insights on the homepage, mobile, 3 times.
Check the LCP element.
6.act: Median LCP 4.8 s. The LCP element is the hero image, which has loading="lazy".

evid.t: Performance 61 · LCP 4.8 s · CLS 0.02 · TBT 90 ms (median of 3)

fix: Remove loading="lazy" from the hero and add fetchpriority="high".
Serve the hero as WebP with srcset.

steps: Open /de/.
Read the CTA in the header and in the hero.
7.act: "Get a quote" (the string was never translated).
fix: Translate the string in the language plugin's string translations.
Run T08.

steps: Open /about/ with the console open.
Wait for the page to load and read the errors.
8.act: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'addEventListener') at slider.js:14

evid.t: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'addEventListener') at slider.js:14

fix: Load slider.js only on pages with a slider, or guard the element with if (el).
8.code:
const el = document.querySelector('.slider');
if (el) el.addEventListener('click', onSlide);

steps: Open the homepage.
Run axe (WCAG 2 A and AA) and filter by serious and critical.
9.act: color-contrast (serious): white text on #ffb648 = 1.9:1 on 2 buttons.
fix: Use dark text #1d2433 on amber (8.9:1), or darken the amber.
9.risk: Brand look: show the option to the owner.

steps: In WebKit, tap "Get a quote".
See where #quote lands under the sticky header.
10.exp: The heading is visible below the header.
10.act: In one WebKit run the heading sat under the 64 px header. Not reproduced in Chromium.

evid.t: WebKit run 1: #quote top = 12 px (under the header); run 2: 70 px

fix: Add html { scroll-padding-top: 72px }.

steps: Ask how release 4.0 was checked.
Look for any CI or uptime check.
11.exp: A short post-deploy check runs after each release.
11.act: No checks: the release went live on Friday and the form bug was found by this audit.

evid.t: Owner's answer: "we look at the homepage after deploy"

fix: Run qa-tests after every deploy (by hand, or in CI on a deploy hook).
Add an uptime monitor for / and /tracking/.
11.risk: Tests that cry wolf get ignored: keep the suite short and fix flaky checks at once.
11.code:
# .github/workflows/qa.yml (after deploy)
- run: cd qa-tests && npm ci && npx playwright install --with-deps chromium && npx playwright test

checklist.note: Clean on 9 of 10 key pages; /about/ has #8.

tests.t: GA4 tag present and sending on /
No sideways scroll at 390 and 820 px
Customs card text is about customs
Quote form: required fields and types
axe: no serious or critical violations
Every sitemap URL answers 200 without a redirect

answers.a: Quote request form, phone click, shipment tracking
Read-only WordPress connector; GA4 via the owner's screen share
Skipped. Assumption: none known, so everything found is new

GA4.d: Google's analytics. Here it counts page views but not leads.

generate_lead.d: GA4's recommended event name for a submitted lead form, usually marked as a key event.

key event.d: An event GA4 treats as a goal (formerly a "conversion"), such as a lead or a call.

dataLayer.d: The array on the page that gtag and GTM read events from. We watch it for new entries.

DebugView.d: A GA4 screen that shows a test device's events in real time.

LCP.d: Largest Contentful Paint: when the biggest block of the first screen appears. Good is 2.5 s or less.

ICE.d: Impact × Confidence × Ease, each from 1 to 10.

pre-mortem.d: Imagine the fix failed and explain why. The reason becomes a step to check.

301.d: Tells browsers and Google a page moved for good; keeps links and rankings.

axe.d: An automated scan for WCAG violations such as low contrast or missing labels.

WCAG.d: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the rules that make sites usable for people with disabilities.

WebKit.d: The browser engine behind Safari; Playwright runs it to test the site as Safari would.

Playwright.d: Opens the site in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit and checks it step by step. The tests are in qa-tests/.

CTA.d: The button that leads to the main action, here "Get a quote".

sitemap.d: The XML list of pages the site asks search engines to index. It should hold only final URLs that answer 200.

hreflang.d: Tags that tell search engines which page is in which language.
